newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says waiting for NAFTA challenge on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Canada says waiting for NAFTA challenge on Cuba.

text.p: International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Thursday that Canada would await developments at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) before challenging Washington's anti-Cuba law under NAFTA.

"I'm waiting to see what happens at the WTO, how that unfolds. And I'm holding this one -- NAFTA -- in reserve. But I'm prepared to use it if we need to. Meanwhile I'll see how it unfolds at the WTO," Eggleton told reporters.
Canada has backed the European Union in going to the WTO to fight the Helms-Burton law, which penalises companies dealing with property in Cuba expropriated from U.S. interests.
It says the law is also illegal under NAFTA, the North American Free Trade Agreement which groups the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Eggleton ridiculed the U.S. for saying the law was justified for national security reasons. He said that may have been true when Cuba was a Soviet ally but said Cuba was now just an island of 10 million people.
The WTO said on Thursday it had chosen the members of a dispute panel to rule on the EU complaint.
